pages.note: Checked once before fetching anything else, per the fetching-etiquette rule.

coverage.why: ra.co/robots.txt names three user-agents under an 'ai content scraping bots' heading and disallows all of them from the entire site: Claude-Web, ClaudeBot, and anthropic-ai (alongside GPTBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot, etc.). I am a Claude/Anthropic agent. The task's fetching instructions supplied a generic browser User-Agent string for plain HTML, and my requests would technically have gone through under the general 'User-agent: *' rule (which allows everything except /pro, /user, /api, /my-tickets, /logout.aspx, /inbox.aspx, /widget) if I'd sent that string -- but the site has separately and explicitly named my own agent family as disallowed. Sending a spoofed browser UA specifically to route around a block that is addressed to me by name is the bypass the task's own etiquette rules forbid ('no bypassing a block ... a source that refuses a gentle reader is itself a finding'). So I did not fetch any ra.co content beyond robots.txt itself -- no event pages, no GraphQL calls, nothing. This is a source-level finding, not a per-venue one: RA is unreachable for this project through any automated Claude-driven fetch (curl, WebFetch, or firecrawl_scrape all identify the request as coming from this agent) unless Kevin (a human) pulls the pages himself, e.g. by browsing ra.co in his own signed-in session and saving/pasting what he sees, or reads them in Chrome via the claude-in-chrome extension backed by his own logged-in browser tab (this pipes through his own browser's real UA and session, not this fetch identity, though the ethics of doing that for a site that has explicitly said no to AI agents are worth Kevin weighing before we lean on it) -- or someone confirms the block doesn't apply to the intended use and asks RA for an exception.
